title: Cap. VIII Arg. 1 Resp. coda (Vasquez): reprobates excluded from God himself without occasion from demerits
pass_a_gloss: Vasquez the Jesuit, who does not greatly favor our defense, yet in this matter votes with us: By that peculiar and efficacious grace, says he, which is proper to the predestined, God without doubt excluded all the reprobate from himself by antecedent will, no occasion at all having been seized from them. For the negation of this grace altogether precedes our liberty. This is to us just as if he had said that God from himself, by antecedent will, no occasion having been seized from their demerits, passed by or reprobated all the reprobate.
pass_b_english: Vasquez the Jesuit — no great friend of our defense — still sides with us here. By that peculiar efficacious grace proper to the predestined, he says, God without doubt excluded all the reprobate from himself by antecedent will, seizing no occasion at all from them. Denial of that grace wholly precedes our liberty. For us that is as good as saying: God from himself, by antecedent will, with no occasion taken from their demerits, passed by or reprobated all the reprobate.
source_text: Vasques Jesuita, qui nostrae defensioni non admodum favet, tamen hac in re nobis suffragatur: Ea gratia, inquit ille, peculiari et efficaci, quae est propria praedestinatorum, Deus absque dubio omnes reprobos ex seipso antecedente voluntate exclusit, nulla prorsus ex ipsis arrepta occasione. Negatio enim hujus gratiae nostram libertatem omnino praecedit. Hoc nobis perinde est ac si dixisset, Deum ex seipso, antecedente voluntate, nulla ex ipsorum demeritis arrepta occasione, omnes reprobos praeteriisse sive reprobasse.
